info.title: Larder API
info.description:
Home inventory: stock, places, shops, shopping lists and scanning.

Authenticate with `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (create tokens in Settings → Access tokens) or the web app session cookie. Errors are `{ error, message }` where `message` is written for people.

bearer.description: An access token from Settings → Access tokens.

get.summary: Where home is, and whether Larder can reach Home Assistant

put.summary: Say where home is: a postcode or town to look up, or a position
put.description: Only needed when Home Assistant doesn't know, or to search from somewhere else. The search text goes to OpenStreetMap's Nominatim.

delete.summary: Forget the home set here and use Home Assistant's again

post.summary: Look for a shop's branches near home on OpenStreetMap
post.description: Answers within about 10 seconds with what it has. If the map servers are busy, Larder keeps trying in the background (after 1, 2, 5, 10, 15 minutes, then every 30, for up to a day) and publishes `shop-locations.found` when it gets an answer. A recent search is answered from what it found unless `again` is set; `now` tries a waiting search straight away. Home's position is rounded to about 1 km before it is sent.

post.summary: Read a photo of something and say what it is (nothing is saved)
post.description: Send a photo as base64 (JPEG, PNG, WebP or GIF; resize it to about 1600 pixels first). The AIs are asked in the household's order; if one can't (out of credit, key refused, busy), the next is asked. The answer fills in the Add item page: check it, then save it as usual.

post.summary: Read a photo of a receipt and match its lines to the household's items (nothing is added)
post.description: Send a photo as base64, as for /identify. Each line comes back matched to an item Larder has, or with none: receipts are often vague, and nothing new is made from one. Lines matched the same way before at that shop are matched without the AI's guess. Send the lines to keep to /receipt/add.

post.summary: Add the lines kept from a receipt to stock, with the prices paid
post.description: All the lines are added or none are. The prices are recorded as prices paid at the shop (the pricing module keeps them), and each line's text is remembered for that shop, so the next receipt matches it straight away.

post.summary: Put a shared link in Pending (from the Home Assistant app's share menu)
post.description: Send what the phone shared: the link, or text with a link in it. Larder reads the page for the product's name, picture and price, and puts it in Pending, to go on the wish list or into Larder. Something already in Pending or in Larder (the same link, or the same name) isn't added again.

get.summary: Shared links waiting in Pending, newest first

post.summary: Put a shared link from Pending on the wish list
A shared link from Pending was added to Larder (through the Add item page): it leaves Pending, and the item keeps where it came from

delete.summary: Forget a shared link in Pending (shared by mistake), and its picture

get.summary: Larder Automations: where it runs (never its token) and its automations, with the shop each is linked to

put.summary: Set where Larder Automations runs, its token and how to wake its Mac (admin)
put.description: The address is the Mac's (port 8700 unless given); the token is from the Larder Automations menu (Copy token). Leave the token out to keep the saved one.

delete.summary: Forget Larder Automations, and the shops linked to its automations (items keep their listings) (admin)

post.summary: Test Larder Automations: is it up, which automations it runs, is the Chrome extension connected (admin)
post.description: With wake: true, wakes the Mac through Home Assistant first if it doesn't answer. Fills in waking from the Mac's network card when it isn't set up.

get.summary: Shopping providers, and the types that can be added

post.summary: Add a shopping provider: link a Larder Automations automation to a shop, or one at its own address (admin)
post.description: One per shop, the first added is the default. For an automation on Larder Automations, give automation (e.g. "tesco"): it uses the hub's address, token and waking. Otherwise give the address it runs at (e.g. 192.168.1.231:8710) and its token (AUTH_TOKEN).

delete.summary: Remove a shopping provider (its items keep their listings) (admin)

post.summary: Test the connection: health and manifest, saved as its status (admin)
post.description: With wake: true, wakes the machine through Home Assistant first if it doesn't answer (this can take a few minutes). Fills in waking from the provider's manifest when it isn't set up.

post.summary: Link a shop's product to an item by its code or link
post.description: Looks the product up with the shop's provider (adding it to the shop's favourites too with addToFavourites), and works out how many of the item one pack gives from its pack size (check it when it says guessed). A code or link the shop doesn't know is refused, never guessed.

patch.summary: Say how many of the item one pack of a listing gives

delete.summary: Unlink a listing from an item

put.summary: Set an item's pack rule and target price at one shop
put.description: packRule: fixed (always one listing, fixedListingId or the first) or cheapest (the cheapest mix of listings that covers what's needed). targetPrice is per one of the item's unit and overrides the item's own (null to use it).

put.summary: Set an item's target price and on-offer stock-up amount
put.description: targetPrice is per one of the item's unit: at or below it counts as on offer, and the order tops up to offerStockUpTo. The normal stock-up amount is the item's own stockUpTo.
